content: Mycobacterium terrae All six isolates from a single center and over 90% of an additional 22 isolates of the Mycobacterium terrae complex were found to be susceptible to ciprofloxacin and sulfonamides. Recently, 11 isolates of the Mycobacterium terrae complex were also shown to be susceptible to linezolid. Mycobacterium szulgai Mycobacterium szulgai is susceptible in vitro to most antituberculous drugs, including quinolones and newer macrolides. Infection 1. Pulmonary infection: A threeor four-drug regimen based on susceptibility testing is recommended, including 12 months of negative sputum cultures while on therapy. 2. Extrapulmonary infection: Combination antituberculous medications based on in vitro susceptibilities should be administered for 4–6 months. Mycobacterium smegmatis Mild disease: The preferred regimen includes doxycycline (oral) and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (oral). Severe disease: The preferred regimen includes amikacin (intravenous) or imipenem (intravenous). Mycobacterium mucogenicum In vitro susceptibility testing shows activity against aminoglycosides, cefoxitin, clarithromycin, minocycline, doxycycline, quinolones, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and imipenem. Mycobacterium malmoense In vitro susceptibility: Ethambutol, ethionamide, kanamycin, and cycloserine are effective. Resistance is noted to isoniazid (INH), streptomycin, rifampin, and capreomycin. Pulmonary infection: The preferred regimen includes isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, with or without quinolones and macrolides. Mycobacterium immunogenum In vitro susceptibility: Susceptible to amikacin and clarithromycin. Resistant to ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, cefoxitin, tobramycin, and sulfamethoxazole. Note: Optimal therapy for this organism is unknown, and successful treatment is challenging due to extensive antibiotic resistance. Mycobacterium leprae Multibacillary leprosy (skin smear positive): Adults: Dapsone 100 mg/day orally, rifampin 600 mg orally four times per week, and clofazimine 50 mg orally daily for 12–24 months. Clofazimine should be supplemented with a loading dose of 300 mg orally monthly. Pediatrics: Dapsone 1–2 mg/kg/day orally and rifampin 450 mg orally for 12–24 months for children under 35 kg. Adjustments are made for children under 20 kg and under 12 kg. Paucibacillary leprosy (skin smear negative): Rifampin 600 mg orally once a month for 6 months and dapsone 100 mg orally daily for 6 months. Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL): Mild cases: Rest, analgesics, and follow-up twice weekly. Chloroquine or aspirin may be useful. Severe cases: Prednisolone 30–40 mg/day orally for 1–2 weeks, then tapered over 12 weeks. Alternative regimens include clofazimine or thalidomide. Reversal reaction: Prednisolone starting at 40 mg/day orally, tapered by 10 mg twice weekly over 12 weeks.
